requirements.notes: subs module per INTERFACE_CONTRACTS 6: monthly/annual plans, trials, coupons, subscribe from the caller's own account under a bank direct-debit mandate, hourly billing, dunning, plan changes with documented proration. Gate test: 7 of 7 scenarios pass (criterion >= 3).
cancel at period end, resume, immediate (customer: no refund; merchant: pro-rata refund), trial cancellation, churn. 6 of 6 scenarios pass (>= 3).

refunds after settlement as reversing ledger entries (kind refund, ref = invoice/purchase, memo names the reversed txn); partial refunds bounded; licence revoked on full refund; refused without merchant funds. 5 of 5 scenarios pass (>= 3).

independent_customers counts distinct economic units with qualifying subscriptions; related_party_exclusion_errors 0 with 15 independent and 8 planted related customers; 15 distinct paying accounts (no pooled household payments).
MRR exact (Fraction), annual / 12, ARR = 12 x MRR; 0 mismatches against an independent recomputation from the event log and ledger at 13 checkpoints; $100k ARR = $8,333.33 MRR.
cash-basis profit = independent revenue - operating - infrastructure costs; reconciliation error 0 cents against the scenario's own bookkeeping, cash reconciliation error 0.

related_flows(world, owner): extended related parties, pro-rata source-of-funds tracing since genesis, reciprocal max-flow netting excluding consideration for goods. 13 planted scheme types (15 payers) all detected; 0 of 40 ordinary customers flagged.

generated startup worlds (800 independent customers with own accounts and 2-5 % monthly voluntary churn, 2-3 incumbents) and a scripted ReferenceSaaS strategy; qualifying ARR >= $100,000 sustained over the last 7 days of 120 on seeds 1 and 3 (min $126,257); idle baseline ARR 0. Uses F1's own individually-accounted customers (patrons), not the v5 population (not merged) and not the 4.0 consumers (aggregate household payments). Marked slow (about 2 minutes).

one scenario per feature: formation, development, subscriptions, one-time purchases, licensing, marketplaces (agent-run exchange with take rate, NPC buyers and sellers choosing), SaaS, education, media, developer tools, data, infrastructure, industrial, contracts, refunds, cancellations, support, competition, bankruptcy (orderly wind-down and insolvency), plus independent-revenue-only. 20 of 20 pass (>= 19).

limitations: Media/entertainment demand is not modelled by the F1 customers (no content understanding here); media products are sold, delivered, consumed and revoked correctly, valuation is left to the social layer (C/D).

Integrity: a colluder with large independent funds reimbursed through consideration for real goods escapes both measures; payments for services or digital goods from a merchant to a customer are netted (conservative: such a supplier-customer is excluded); reciprocal search capped at 256 payer groups (reported as truncated).
Source-of-funds tracing replays the whole ledger per merchant (linear, cached per world sequence number); fine for evaluator use, not meant as a per-step reward signal at internet scale.
Profit is cash basis (capex counted when paid, no depreciation).
Billing months are 30 days, years 365 days; no calendar. Goods are not sold by subscription.
The admission harness's random session exercises few successful calls of these modules; determinism is additionally covered by a 70-day customer economy that replays, regenerates and forks exactly.
